newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms further on IMF agreement.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms further on IMF agreement.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev kept gaining on the local interbank market on Monday following approval of a $657 million credit package for Bulgaria by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), traders said.

The lev rose to 1,480-1,500 per dollar at midday from 1,480-1,530 at the opening and 1,522-1,530 at Friday's close as dollar supply rose on profit-taking and in anticipation of further lev gains now that Bulgaria has won IMF support.
"Final clients are actively offering dollars, expecting the lev to advance further or at least trade stable around current levels but there are almost no bidders," one dealer said.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was seen as the main dollar buyer in the morning, containing the lev rise, dealers said. BNB officials were not available for comment.

The IMF board late on Friday approved a $657 million credit package for Bulgaria, including a 14-month $509 million stand-by facility to support the country's move towards market economy and make up for a serious decline in its cereal yields.
Under the agreement with the IMF Bulgaria is to set up in June a fixed exchange rate regime, a currency board mechanism, to restore confidence in the lev and stabilise its crumbling financial system.

The mechanism would require levs in circulation to be matched with the country's foreign exchange reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the central bank and the government and preventing the printing of money. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
